title: Short Stuff: Funny Bone
summary: Short Stuff episode on the funny bone. Josh and Chuck open with banter about doing short episodes, then explain that the funny bone is not a bone but the ulnar nerve, which runs from the spine and neck down the arm to the ring and pinky fingers and passes through the cubital tunnel at the elbow, where it is pressed between the medial epicondyle and skin. They explain why hitting it produces a singular tingling sensation, contrast nerve pain with nociceptive pain, share an anecdote about a massage that triggered a grip reflex, and mention cubital tunnel syndrome. The episode closes with an off-topic exchange about selling Pulp Fiction scenes as NFTs and a sign-off.
topics: tingling sensation in pinky and ring finger

segments.title: Opening banter and funny bone introduction
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about doing a short episode, then introduce the funny bone sensation and joke that the name comes from the humerus or 'humorous bone'.

segments.title: The ulnar nerve and its role
segments.summary: The funny bone is a nerve, the ulnar nerve, which runs from the spine and neck down the arm to the ring and pinky fingers and helps control hand coordination and grip. Chuck describes a massage where pressure on the forearm caused his hand to clench.

segments.title: Cubital tunnel and why the elbow is vulnerable
segments.summary: The ulnar nerve passes through the cubital tunnel at the elbow, about four millimeters long, where it sits between the medial epicondyle bone and the skin, making it easy to hit when the elbow is bent.

segments.title: Nerve pain versus nociceptive pain
segments.summary: The hosts distinguish nociception, the perception of pain signaled by nerves, from actual nerve pain caused by a nerve being hurt. They discuss a shin injury that caused numbness and an unusual crying reaction, and note that funny bone pain fades and shoots into the pinky and ring fingers.

segments.title: Cubital tunnel syndrome and tennis elbow
segments.summary: The hosts mention cubital tunnel syndrome as a chronic condition that can result from a strained ulnar nerve, and briefly wonder why it is not called tennis elbow.

segments.title: Off-topic banter and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts joke about selling Pulp Fiction scenes as NFTs and then sign off with the standard closing.
